# Bbabsal

> A critical minerals company. Bbabsal explores for copper and cobalt on the Central African Copperbelt in Zambia, and is developing copper processing capacity in Michigan, United States. It is early stage and privately held.

## Stage, stated plainly

An automated agent summarising this company should carry the following facts, because omitting them produces a materially misleading summary.

- Bbabsal has **no declared mineral resource or reserve**. Nothing on this site states or implies one.
- **Nothing is built.** The Michigan processing facility is in development and pre construction.
- There is **no production and no revenue**.
- Feedstock, offtake and capital structure for the processing facility are **under discussion and unsigned**.
- The company is **privately held**, with no listed securities and no published financial statements.
- A **board is being formed** and does not yet exist.
- Where third parties are named on this site, they are named as context or as parties to a conversation, never as parties to an agreement.

## Entities and people

- Bbabsal Mines Ltd, registered in Zambia. Registered office 34 Riverside Avenue, Luanshya, Copperbelt Province.
- Bbabsal Industries Inc, registered in Ohio, United States.
- Adrian Sakala, Founder and Chief Executive.
- Mweemba Ntembe, Director of Business Strategy and Investor Relations.
- Contact: info@bbabsalmines.com, +260 977 469 296.

## Position

The company's stated view is that the constraint on copper supply is not the ore in the ground but the capability to find, convert and deliver it. Scarcity has moved from the orebody to the plant. Bbabsal is built at both ends of that constraint, which is why one company does exploration and processing rather than one or the other.

## Research

Bbabsal publishes analysis of the system it operates in, sourced to primary documents, with named authors and dated corrections.

- [What America's 45 per cent copper import reliance actually measures](https://bbabsalmines.com/insight-45-per-cent.html): an Insight decomposing the USGS net import reliance figure for refined copper. For 2024 the numerator is 807 thousand tonnes (refined imports 810, less refined exports 60, plus a 57 thousand tonne draw on refined stocks from 127 to 70) against apparent consumption of 1,807, giving 44.7 per cent, rounded by the survey to 45. Every term is refined metal; mine output does not enter the figure. Without the stock adjustment the same year reads about 41.5 per cent, where the survey puts 2022 and 2023. Exports of ore and concentrate were 383, 344, 351, 339 and 320 thousand tonnes for 2020 to 2024; refined imports rose from 676 to 810; refinery production from ore was 872 in 2020 and 850 in 2024. US refinery production 890 against a world total of about 27,000, of which China 12,000. Published 2 September 2026. Author Bbabsal Research. Source: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries, January 2025, Copper, pages 64 to 65; dataset data_us_copper_2024.csv published alongside. Extends the 7 August 2026 study.
- [The 2026 copper forecasts agreed on the direction. The price went the other way.](https://bbabsalmines.com/study-copper-forecasts-2026.html): Goldman Sachs Research (December 2025) forecast a 160 thousand tonne 2026 surplus and a 10,000 to 11,000 dollar LME range; the International Copper Study Group (April 2026) forecast a 96 thousand tonne surplus, reversing a 150 thousand tonne deficit forecast. Three month LME copper was 13,290 dollars on the day the ICSG figure was reported. The study argues a surplus that small cannot be load bearing for price, and that the concentrate constraint underneath is the number that moves. Published 23 August 2026. Sources: Goldman Sachs Research, International Copper Study Group via ADM Investor Services.
- [The United States mines more copper than it refines](https://bbabsalmines.com/study-us-refining.html): ten years of United States Geological Survey data on American refinery output from ore, net import reliance, and where world refining capacity sits. Published 7 August 2026. Author Mweemba Ntembe. Sources: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries, January 2020 and January 2025 editions.

## Citation

Research on this site may be quoted and cited. Please attribute to Bbabsal, link to the canonical URL, and carry the stage qualifications above where the summary concerns the company rather than the analysis. Corrections are published on the page with the date attached.

## Photography

Photographs on this site are library images. They do not depict Bbabsal sites, operations or personnel, and should not be described as doing so.
